The team must receive AWS Health events for all accounts in the organization in one place, without deploying rules to every account. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Keep the current rule, because EventBridge rules for AWS Health receive events for every account in the organization.
Deploy the same EventBridge rule to every member account with StackSets, and have each rule send email to the team.
Ask each account owner to check the AWS Health Dashboard every day and forward important events.
Use the AWS Health organizational view with delegated administrator access for the operations account to aggregate events from all accounts.

explanation.summary: Health のイベントの EventBridge のルールは、自分のアカウントの通知しか受けない。組織の他のアカウントのイベントを受けるには、組織のビュー（organizational view）と委任管理者のアクセスで Health のイベントを集約する。

per_choice.A: ルールが受けるのは自分のアカウントの通知だけ。
per_choice.B: 全アカウントにルールを置くことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 人の作業に頼ることになり、手間が大きく漏れも出る。
per_choice.D: 正しい。組織のビューと委任管理者で、全アカウントのイベントを 1 か所に集められる。

references.quote: Any EventBridge rules that you create can only receive notifications for your AWS account.
To receive organizational events for other accounts within your AWS Organizations, see Aggregating AWS Health events using organizational view and delegated administrator access.

questions.stem: A web store account (111122223333) must send newOrderCreated events with the source com.exampleCorp.webStore to a central event bus named central-event-bus in a separate account (123456789012). The central account must accept only these events from the web store account, following least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST privilege?

choices.text: Attach a resource-based policy to the event bus in the web store account that allows account 123456789012 to read the events.
Attach a resource-based policy to central-event-bus that allows every account in the organization to publish any event.
Attach a resource-based policy to central-event-bus in account 123456789012 that allows account 111122223333 to publish only events with that source and detail-type.
Create an IAM user in account 123456789012 and store its access keys in the web store application to call PutEvents.

explanation.summary: 別アカウントのイベントバスへ送るには、受け取る側（バスの持ち主）のアカウントのイベントバスにリソースベースのポリシーを付け、送る側のアカウントに発行を許す。条件で source と detail-type を絞れば、決めたイベントだけを受け付けられる。

per_choice.A: ポリシーは受け取る側のバスに付ける。送る側のバスに付けても、中央のバスへの発行は許されない。
per_choice.B: 全てのアカウントの全てのイベントを許すことになり、最小権限に反する。
per_choice.C: 正しい。受け取る側のバスで、送る側のアカウントに、決めたイベントだけの発行を許す。
per_choice.D: 長く使う認証情報をアプリに持たせることになり、最小権限の考え方にも合わない。

references.quote: but only for events with a source value set to com.exampleCorp.webStore and a detail-type set to newOrderCreated.
You attach this resource-based policy to the central-event-bus in the bus-owner account (123456789012), which is the account that receives the events.

questions.stem: A Lambda function processes messages from an Amazon SQS standard queue through an event source mapping. The team is raising the function timeout to 3 minutes. Messages that keep failing must go to a dead-letter queue, but only after Lambda has had a few chances to retry them. The team wants to follow AWS recommendations. Which settings should the team use? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Set the source queue's visibility timeout to 18 minutes.
Set maxReceiveCount in the source queue's redrive policy to 5.
Keep the source queue's visibility timeout at 30 seconds, because Lambda manages visibility itself.
Set maxReceiveCount in the source queue's redrive policy to 1 so that failures reach the dead-letter queue quickly.
Set the function timeout to 20 minutes, longer than the queue's visibility timeout.

explanation.summary: キューの可視性タイムアウトは、関数のタイムアウトの少なくとも 6 倍にするのが勧められている（3 分なら 18 分）。関数のタイムアウトは可視性タイムアウト以下でなければならず、超えるとイベントソースマッピングの作成や更新でエラーになる。デッドレターキューへ送る前に数回やり直せるよう、maxReceiveCount は少なくとも 5 にするのが勧められている。

per_choice.A: 正しい。3 分の 6 倍で 18 分。
per_choice.B: 正しい。数回やり直してからデッドレターキューへ送る。
per_choice.C: 関数のタイムアウトは可視性タイムアウト以下である必要があり、3 分の関数では設定できない。
per_choice.D: やり直さずにすぐデッドレターキューへ送られ、数回やり直す要件に反する。
per_choice.E: 関数のタイムアウトは可視性タイムアウト以下である必要がある。

references.quote: set the source queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the configuration timeout on your function.
Your function's timeout must be less than or equal to the queue's visibility timeout.
We recommend setting the maxReceiveCount on your source queue's redrive policy to at least 5.

questions.stem: A Lambda function receives batches of 10 messages from an Amazon SQS standard queue. When one message in a batch fails, all 10 messages become visible again and are processed again, which creates duplicate records downstream. The team must keep the batch size of 10 for throughput and avoid reprocessing messages that already succeeded. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Throw an exception from the function whenever any message in the batch fails.
Increase the queue's visibility timeout so that failed batches wait longer before they are retried.
Turn on ReportBatchItemFailures on the event source mapping, and return the IDs of the failed messages in batchItemFailures.
Set the batch size to 1 so that each failure affects only one message.

explanation.summary: 既定では、関数がバッチの処理で誤ると、うまく処理したメッセージも含めてバッチの全てのメッセージがキューに見えるようになる。イベントソースマッピングで ReportBatchItemFailures を指定し、応答の batchItemFailures に失敗したメッセージの ID を返すと、失敗した物だけがやり直される。関数が例外を投げると、バッチ全体が失敗とみなされる。

per_choice.A: 例外を投げるとバッチ全体が失敗とみなされ、今と同じになる。
per_choice.B: やり直すまでの時間が延びるだけで、成功したメッセージもやり直される。
per_choice.C: 正しい。失敗したメッセージだけがやり直される。
per_choice.D: バッチの大きさ 10 を保つ要件に反する。

references.quote: To turn on partial batch responses, specify ReportBatchItemFailures for the FunctionResponseTypes action when configuring your event source mapping.
If your function throws an exception, the entire batch is considered a complete failure.
all messages in that batch become visible in the queue again by default, including messages that Lambda processed successfully.

questions.stem: A Lambda function processes a Kinesis data stream that has four shards, and the function is falling behind. Records with the same partition key must still be processed in order. The team does not want to change the stream, and wants the function to process more batches from each shard at the same time. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Set the event source mapping's ParallelizationFactor to 10.
Set the event source mapping's ParallelizationFactor to 20.
Add shards to the data stream so that Lambda can process more records at once.
Send the records to an Amazon SQS standard queue and process them from the queue instead.

explanation.summary: Lambda は各シャードのレコードを順に処理する。ParallelizationFactor（1〜10、既定 1）を上げると、1 つのシャードから同時に処理するバッチを増やせ、その場合も同じパーティションキーの中では順序が保たれる。シャードを足しても速くできるが、ストリームを変えることになる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。各シャードから同時に 10 バッチまで処理し、キーごとの順序は保たれる。
per_choice.B: ParallelizationFactor は 10 まで。
per_choice.C: ストリームを変えない要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 仕組みを作り直すことになり、キーごとの順序も保てない。

references.quote: You can specify the number of concurrent batches that Lambda polls from a shard by using a parallelization factor from 1 (default) to 10.
When you increase the number of concurrent batches per shard, Lambda still ensures in-order processing at the partition-key level.
To increase the speed at which your function processes records, add shards to your data stream.

questions.note: 選択肢 D の「キーごとの順序を保てない」は SQS standard の性質で、この束の sources には無い

questions.stem: An orders topic in Amazon SNS fans out to three Amazon SQS queues. The shipping team's queue must receive only orders whose message body contains "region": "EU". The publisher does not set any message attributes and cannot be changed. The other two queues must keep receiving every order. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Assign a filter policy with the MessageAttributes scope to the shipping queue's subscription, matching region EU.
Assign a filter policy with the MessageBody scope to the shipping queue's subscription, matching region EU.
Let the shipping consumer read every message and delete the ones whose region is not EU.
Create a separate SNS topic for EU orders and ask the publisher to send EU orders to it.

explanation.summary: SNS のトピックの購読者は、既定では全てのメッセージを受け取る。一部だけを受けるには購読にフィルターポリシーを付ける。範囲（scope）が MessageBody なら、ポリシーの名前はメッセージの本文のプロパティに合わせ、MessageAttributes ならメッセージ属性の名前に合わせる。

per_choice.A: 発行する側はメッセージ属性を付けていないので、合うメッセージが無い。
per_choice.B: 正しい。本文の region で絞り、他の 2 つの購読はそのまま全て受け取る。
per_choice.C: 全てのメッセージを受けて捨てることになり、手間とむだがある。
per_choice.D: 発行する側を変えられない要件に反する。

references.quote: To receive only a subset of the messages, a subscriber must assign a filter policy to the topic subscription.
When the filter policy scope is set to MessageBody, each property name in the filter policy matches a message body property name.
When the filter policy scope is set to MessageAttributes, each property name in the filter policy matches a message attribute name.

questions.stem: A company wants to turn on a new checkout feature in production without redeploying application code. The change must reach users gradually. If a CloudWatch alarm on checkout errors goes off while the change is rolling out, or during a monitoring period after it reaches all targets, the change must be reverted automatically. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Store the flag as an AWS Lambda environment variable, and use a CodeDeploy canary deployment to publish a new function version.
Use an AWS AppConfig feature flag with a gradual deployment strategy that has a bake time, and attach the CloudWatch alarm as a rollback monitor.
Store the flag in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and have an operator change it back if the alarm goes off.
Build a new container image with the flag enabled, and roll it out with an ECS rolling update.

explanation.summary: AWS AppConfig は、コードを配り直さずに本番のアプリの動きを変え、機能を少しずつ広げられる。デプロイ戦略と CloudWatch のアラームによる自動ロールバックを組み合わせると、配信の間にアラームが鳴った時に前の版へ戻す。bake time は、100% に配った後もアラームを見る時間で、その間に鳴っても戻す。

per_choice.A: 関数の新しい版を配ることになり、コードを配り直さない要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 正しい。少しずつ配り、配信中と bake time の間にアラームが鳴れば自動で戻る。
per_choice.C: 戻すのが人の作業になり、自動で戻す要件に合わない。少しずつ広げることもできない。
per_choice.D: コードを作り直して配ることになり、要件に反する。

references.quote: AWS AppConfig helps you safely change application behavior in production without redeploying code.
If an alarm is triggered during this time, AWS AppConfig rolls back the deployment.
using a combination of AWS AppConfig deployment strategies and automatic rollbacks based on Amazon CloudWatch alarms.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer configures AWS AppConfig deployments with CloudWatch alarms as rollback monitors. The team wants to understand exactly when a rollback happens and what it needs, so that it can rely on the feature instead of watching each deployment. Which statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: If a monitored alarm enters ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA during a deployment, AWS AppConfig reverts to the previous configuration data.
AWS AppConfig needs permissions to be configured before it can roll back deployments based on CloudWatch alarms.
AWS AppConfig rolls back only after an operator approves the rollback in the console.
A rollback redeploys the previous version of the application code to the compute targets.
AWS AppConfig stops monitoring alarms as soon as the configuration reaches 100% of its targets.

explanation.summary: 配信の間に見張るアラームが ALARM か INSUFFICIENT_DATA になると、AppConfig は設定のデータを前の版へ自動で戻す。CloudWatch のアラームで戻すには、AppConfig に権限を設定しておく必要がある。100% に配った後も bake time の間はアラームを見続ける。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ALARM と INSUFFICIENT_DATA の両方で戻す。
per_choice.B: 正しい。戻すための権限を設定する必要がある。
per_choice.C: 自動で戻る。人の承認は要らない。
per_choice.D: 戻すのは設定のデータで、アプリのコードではない。
per_choice.E: 100% に配った後も、bake time の間はアラームを見る。

references.quote: if one or more CloudWatch alarms go into the ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATAstate during a deployment, AWS AppConfig automatically rolls back your configuration data to the previous version
You must configure permissions for AWS AppConfig to roll back based on CloudWatch alarms.
This setting specifies the amount of time AWS AppConfig monitors for Amazon CloudWatch alarms after the configuration has been deployed to 100% of its targets

questions.stem: When the Systems Manager parameter /app/db-endpoint is updated, the company must restart the application on a fleet of instances so that they read the new value. A senior engineer must approve each restart before it happens, and the company does not want to write or host custom code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event that invokes an AWS Lambda function, which emails the engineer and waits for a reply before restarting.
Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event, with a Systems Manager Automation runbook as the target that restarts the application immediately.
Have the engineer check the parameter history every morning and restart the application by hand when the value has changed.
Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event, with a Systems Manager Automation runbook as the target that includes an aws:approve step before the restart.

explanation.summary: Parameter Store のパラメータの作成・更新・削除を EventBridge で受け、ルールのターゲットに Automation のランブックを指定すれば、イベントに応じて自動化を始められる。aws:approve のアクションは、決めた人が承認か拒否をするまで自動化を一時停止する。

per_choice.A: 自分でコードを書いて動かすことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 承認の手順が無く、承認してから再起動する要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 人が毎朝確かめることになり、手間が大きく、反映も遅れる。
per_choice.D: 正しい。更新を受けてランブックを始め、承認を待ってから再起動する。

references.quote: Notify you when a parameter or a parameter label version is created, updated, or deleted.
You can start an automation by specifying a runbook as the target of an Amazon EventBridge event.
The automation uses the automation action aws:approve, which temporarily pauses the automation until the designated principals either approve or deny the action.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer must run a Systems Manager Automation runbook that changes a configuration file on 400 managed instances. No more than 20 instances may run the change at the same time. The company allows up to 5 instances to fail; after that, Systems Manager must stop sending the change to the remaining instances. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Run the automation with adaptive concurrency so that Systems Manager raises the number of concurrent runs automatically.
Run the automation with rate control, set the concurrency to 20, and set the error threshold to 5.
Write a script that starts the runbook on 20 instances, waits, counts failures, and repeats until all instances are done.
Run the automation one instance at a time from the console, and stop when 5 instances have failed.

explanation.summary: rate control の concurrency は、同時に自動化を動かしてよいリソースの数を決める。error threshold は、他のリソースへ送るのを止めるまでに失敗してよい自動化の数を決める。adaptive concurrency は、同時の数を 100 から 500 まで自動で増やす物。

per_choice.A: 同時の数を自動で増やす物で、同時に 20 までに抑える要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 正しい。concurrency で同時に動かす数を 20 にし、error threshold で止めるまでに許す失敗の数を 5 にする。
per_choice.C: 自分でスクリプトを作ることになり、手間が大きい。
per_choice.D: 1 台ずつの手作業になり、手間が大きい。

references.quote: The concurrency value determines how many resources are allowed to run the automation simultaneously.
An error threshold determines how many automations are allowed to fail before Systems Manager stops sending the automation to other resources.
Adaptive concurrency automatically scales your automation quota from 100 concurrently running automations up to 500.

questions.stem: Before an Auto Scaling group terminates an instance during scale-in, the company must copy the instance's local logs to Amazon S3. The copy usually takes 20 minutes but can take up to 3 hours for large instances. Termination must wait until the copy finishes. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Add a termination lifecycle hook, start the copy from an EventBridge rule, record heartbeats while the copy runs, and then complete the lifecycle action.
Add a termination lifecycle hook with the default timeout, and start the copy from an EventBridge rule.
Add a termination lifecycle hook, start the copy from an EventBridge rule, and complete the action with ABANDON when the copy starts.
Run a cron job on each instance that copies the logs every hour, and let scale-in terminate instances normally.

explanation.summary: 終了のライフサイクルフックは、縮小の時にインスタンスを終了の前に止め、EventBridge で知らせる。既定の待ち時間は 1 時間（heartbeat timeout）で、時間が足りなければ heartbeat を記録して待ち時間をやり直せる。フックが時間切れになるか abandon にされると、すぐに終了へ進む。

per_choice.A: 正しい。heartbeat で待ち時間を延ばし、コピーが終わってから進める。
per_choice.B: 既定の 1 時間を超えると、コピーの途中でも終了へ進む。
per_choice.C: フックを abandon にすると、すぐに終了へ進むので、コピーが終わる前にインスタンスが終了する。
per_choice.D: 最後の 1 時間までのログが失われうる。

references.quote: When a scale-in event occurs, a lifecycle hook pauses the instance before it is terminated and sends you a notification using Amazon EventBridge.
If you need more time, you can restart the timeout period by recording a heartbeat.
If a termination lifecycle hook times out, or is abandoned, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling proceeds with terminating the instance immediately.

questions.stem: An Auto Scaling group with a desired capacity of 20 instances must move to a new launch template version. During the update, at least 90 percent of the desired capacity must stay in service, the group must not launch extra instances above the desired capacity, and the update should replace 2 instances at a time. Which instance refresh settings BEST meet these requirements?

choices.text: Minimum healthy percentage 100 and maximum healthy percentage 100.
Minimum healthy percentage 0 and maximum healthy percentage 100.
Minimum healthy percentage 50 and maximum healthy percentage 100.
Minimum healthy percentage 90 and maximum healthy percentage 100.

explanation.summary: 最小の正常率は、更新の間に動かし続ける希望の容量の割合。最小 90% と最大 100% なら、一度に容量の 10% を入れ替える（20 台なら 2 台）。最小と最大を両方 100% にすると 1 台ずつ、最小 0% にすると全部を一度に入れ替える。

per_choice.A: 1 台ずつの入れ替えになり、2 台ずつの要件に合わない。
per_choice.B: 全部を一度に入れ替え、90% を保てない。
per_choice.C: 一度に 10 台を入れ替え、90% を保てない。
per_choice.D: 正しい。20 台の 10% で 2 台ずつ入れ替え、90% を保つ。

references.quote: For example, if the minimum healthy percentage is 90 percent and the maximum healthy percentage is 100 percent, then 10 percent of capacity will be replaced at a time.
To replace one instance at a time, set both the minimum and maximum healthy percentage to 100 percent.
To replace all instances at once, set a minimum healthy percentage of 0 percent.

questions.stem: A team runs an instance refresh for an Auto Scaling group. The team wants to be notified when 20 percent of the instances have been replaced so that it can check the application, and wants every replaced instance to be reverted automatically if a CloudWatch alarm on errors goes into ALARM during the refresh. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Set checkpoints at 20 percent and 100 percent, and use an EventBridge rule to send checkpoint events to Amazon SNS.
Turn on auto rollback for the instance refresh and specify the CloudWatch alarm.
Cancel the instance refresh if the alarm goes off, because canceling restores the replaced instances.
Wait until the instance refresh finishes, and then roll it back if the alarm went off.
Set a single checkpoint at 20 percent, which also completes the refresh after the team confirms.

explanation.summary: チェックポイントは、新しいインスタンスが何 % になったら止まるかを決め、100% 以外のチェックポイントごとにイベントを出す。EventBridge のルールで SNS などへ送れる。複数のチェックポイントを使う時は、全て入れ替えるために最後を 100% にする。自動のロールバックは、更新が失敗するか指定したアラームが ALARM になった時に元へ戻す。取り消しや失敗で止まっても、入れ替えた物は戻らず、終わった後はロールバックできない。

per_choice.A: 正しい。20% で知らせ、最後は 100% にして全て入れ替える。
per_choice.B: 正しい。アラームが ALARM になれば自動で元へ戻す。
per_choice.C: 取り消しても、既に入れ替えたインスタンスは元に戻らない。
per_choice.D: 終わった後のインスタンスのリフレッシュはロールバックできない。
per_choice.E: 複数のチェックポイントでは最後を 100% にする必要がある。20% だけでは全て入れ替わらない。

references.quote: You can add an EventBridge rule to send the events to a target such as Amazon SNS.
If you cancel the operation or it fails before reaching the last checkpoint, any instances that were already replaced are not rolled back to their previous configuration.
Auto rollback: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically reverses what was deployed if the instance refresh fails for some reason or if any CloudWatch alarms you specify go into the ALARM state.
You can't roll it back after it's finished.

questions.stem: During an incident, engineers changed several security group rules directly in the console, although the security groups are managed by an AWS CloudFormation stack. The team now needs to find which stack resources were changed outside of CloudFormation and which properties differ from the template, without changing any resources. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create a change set with the current template and review the resources that the change set would modify.
Run drift detection on the stack and review the drifted resources and their properties.
Update the stack with the same template so that CloudFormation lists the resources it restores.
Review the stack events list to find the resources whose rules were changed in the console.

explanation.summary: ドリフト検出は、CloudFormation の管理の外で設定が変えられたスタックのリソースを見つけ、実際の設定が期待される設定と違うかを調べる。1 つ以上のプロパティが消されたり値を変えられたりしたリソースはドリフトしたとみなされる。

per_choice.A: change set はテンプレートの変更で何が変わるかを見る物で、管理の外の変更を調べる物ではない。
per_choice.B: 正しい。リソースを変えずに、管理の外で変わったリソースとプロパティを見つける。
per_choice.C: リソースに手を入れることになり、何も変えない要件に反する。
per_choice.D: スタックのイベントは CloudFormation の操作の記録で、コンソールでの直接の変更は出ない。

references.quote: You can use drift detection to identify stack resources to which configuration changes have been made outside of CloudFormation management.
A resource is considered to have drifted if one or more of its properties have been deleted, or had their value changed.

questions.note: 選択肢 B・C・D の説明は、この束の sources に直接の原文は無い（C-0018 の change sets の出典 S1 で B を言える）

questions.stem: An in-place AWS CodeDeploy deployment to Amazon EC2 instances fails in the ApplicationStop lifecycle event. The logs show that the ApplicationStop script has a bug. The team fixed the script in the new revision, but the next deployment fails in ApplicationStop with the same error. The team must deploy the fixed revision as soon as possible without logging in to the instances. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create a deployment of the fixed revision with the --ignore-application-stop-failures option.
Deploy the same fixed revision again, because CodeDeploy runs ApplicationStop from the revision that is being deployed.
Roll back to the last successful revision, and then deploy the fixed revision again without changes.
Reinstall the CodeDeploy agent on every instance so that it downloads the new ApplicationStop script.

explanation.summary: CodeDeploy のエージェントは、ApplicationStop・BeforeBlockTraffic・AfterBlockTraffic のスクリプトを、前に成功したデプロイの AppSpec から動かす。新しいリビジョンでスクリプトを直しても、前の成功したデプロイのスクリプトが動くので同じ所で失敗する。そのスクリプトが必ず失敗するなら、失敗を無視するデプロイを作る（CLI の --ignore-application-stop-failures）。

per_choice.A: 正しい。前のデプロイの壊れたスクリプトの失敗を無視して、直したリビジョンを配れる。
per_choice.B: ApplicationStop は前に成功したデプロイのスクリプトから動くので、同じ失敗がくり返す。
per_choice.C: 前の成功したリビジョンに戻っても、そのリビジョンの壊れたスクリプトが次の ApplicationStop で動き、同じ所で失敗する。
per_choice.D: どのスクリプトを動かすかは前に成功したデプロイで決まるので、エージェントを入れ直しても変わらない。

references.quote: the CodeDeploy agent runs the scripts specified for ApplicationStop, BeforeBlockTraffic, and AfterBlockTraffic in the AppSpec file from the previous successful deployment.
Use the AWS CLI to call the create-deployment command and include the --ignore-application-stop-failures option.

questions.stem: An AWS CloudFormation stack update failed, and the rollback also failed. The stack is now in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state because a dependent resource could not return to its original state. The team found and manually fixed the cause of the failure. The team wants to return the stack to a working state and then apply the update again, without deleting the stack. What should the team do next with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Run a new stack update with the original template, because updates are allowed in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state.
Wait for CloudFormation to retry the rollback automatically after the resource is fixed.
Continue the update rollback so that the stack reaches UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, and then update the stack again.
Delete the stack and create it again from the new template.

explanation.summary: 依存するリソースが元の状態に戻れないとロールバックが失敗し、UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED になる。原因を手で直したら、ロールバックを続ける（continue update rollback）と UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE の動く状態に戻り、そこからもう一度更新できる。それでも戻せないリソースは飛ばせる。

per_choice.A: まずロールバックを続けて動く状態に戻す必要がある。
per_choice.B: ロールバックを続けるのは、コンソールか CLI で行う操作。
per_choice.C: 正しい。ロールバックを続けて UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE にしてから、もう一度更新する。
per_choice.D: スタックを消さない要件に反する。

references.quote: By continuing the rollback, you can return your stack to a working state (the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE state), and then try to update the stack again.
To continue rolling back an update, you can use the CloudFormation console or AWS command line interface (AWS CLI).

questions.note: 選択肢 A・C の「できない」は、S3 の手順（まずロールバックを続ける）から言える範囲で書いた

questions.stem: A pipeline stage runs three test actions in parallel. Occasionally one action fails because of a short network problem while the other two succeed. The team wants to rerun only the failed action without starting the pipeline from the beginning or rerunning the successful actions. The team also wants the stage to be retried automatically once when it fails. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Use Retry failed actions on the stage when an action fails.
Configure automatic retry on stage failure for the stage, with one retry attempt.
Use Retry failed stage, which reruns only the actions that failed.
Choose Release change to run the pipeline again from the source stage.
Configure automatic retry on stage failure with three retry attempts to cover longer problems.

explanation.summary: 失敗した段階は、パイプラインを最初から動かさずにやり直せる。失敗したアクションをやり直す（retry failed actions）と、失敗したアクションだけが動き直す。失敗した段階をやり直す（retry failed stage）と、段階の最初のアクションから全てが動き直す。段階の失敗の自動のやり直しは、1 回だけ設定できる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。失敗したアクションだけがもう一度動く。
per_choice.B: 正しい。自動のやり直しは 1 回だけ設定できる。
per_choice.C: retry failed stage は段階の全てのアクションを最初からやり直す。
per_choice.D: パイプラインを最初から動かすことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.E: 自動のやり直しは 1 回までしか設定できない。

references.quote: Retrying a failed stage retries all actions in the stage from the first action in the stage, and retrying failed actions retries all failed actions in the stage.
You can only configure automatic retry on stage failure for one retry attempt.
You can retry a stage that has failed without having to run a pipeline again from the beginning.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer creates a new AWS CodePipeline pipeline and configures automatic rollback on failure for the Deploy stage. The very first execution of the pipeline fails in the Deploy stage, but no rollback happens. The engineer wants to understand the behavior before changing anything. Which statement BEST explains why the stage did not roll back?

choices.text: Automatic rollback is supported only for stages that contain AWS CodeDeploy actions.
Automatic rollback must also be configured on the source stage before it can work on the Deploy stage.
Automatic rollback works only after the stage has had at least one successful execution to roll back to.
Automatic rollback runs only when the stage is retried by hand after the failure.

explanation.summary: 段階が失敗すると、その段階は最も新しい成功した実行に戻される。自動のロールバックはパイプラインの定義の一部なので、その段階で成功した実行が 1 回あった後にしか戻せない。また、戻せるのは今のパイプラインの構造の版で始まった実行だけ。

per_choice.A: この条件は無い。戻らない理由は、成功した実行が無いこと。
per_choice.B: ソースの段階の設定は関係ない。戻らない理由は、成功した実行が無いこと。
per_choice.C: 正しい。最初の実行では、戻る先の成功した実行が無い。
per_choice.D: 段階が失敗した時に自動で戻す仕組みで、手でやり直すことは条件ではない。

references.quote: When the stage fails, the stage is rolled back to the most recent successful execution.
your pipeline stage will auto-rollback only after there is a successful pipeline execution in the pipeline stage.

questions.stem: Shortly after a new application version is deployed, a CloudWatch Synthetics canary that tests the checkout flow starts to fail. Customers are affected. The team must restore service quickly and must still be able to find the root cause afterward. Which approach BEST meets these requirements?

choices.text: Keep the new version, compare the failed run's screenshots and logs with a successful run, and roll back only if the cause is unclear.
Check the SuccessPercent metric over the next hour to see whether failures are intermittent, and then decide whether to roll back.
Roll back the recent deployment, and delete the failed canary runs' artifacts so that the next runs start from a clean state.
Roll back the recent deployment, and then compare the failed run's screenshots, logs, and step reports with a successful run.

explanation.summary: canary が失敗した時は、詳細のページの SuccessPercent で続く問題か時々の問題かを見て、失敗した回のスクリーンショット・ログ・ステップの報告を成功した回と比べて原因を絞る。直前にアプリをデプロイしていたなら、まず戻してから後で調べる。

per_choice.A: 原因は調べられるが、新しい版のまま利用者への影響が続き、早く戻す要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 続く問題か時々の問題かは分かるが、判断まで利用者への影響が続き、早く戻す要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 早く戻せるが、失敗した回の記録を消すので、後から成功した回と比べて原因を調べられなくなる。
per_choice.D: 正しい。まず戻して利用者への影響を止め、canary の記録で後から原因を調べる。

references.quote: If you had a recent deployment to your application, roll it back and then debug later.
Finally, you can compare these artifacts with the artifacts from a successful canary run to pinpoint the issue.

questions.stem: A company lets developers create IAM roles for their AWS Lambda functions in a shared account. Any role that a developer creates must never be able to do more than read and write one Amazon S3 bucket and one Amazon DynamoDB table. Other teams in the same account need broader permissions. The security team does not want to review each role by hand. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary to each developer that allows the S3 and DynamoDB access, and give the Lambda roles no other policies.
Apply an SCP to the account that denies every action except the S3 and DynamoDB access.
Create a managed policy that allows only the S3 and DynamoDB access, and allow developers to create roles only when that policy is attached as the permissions boundary.
Give developers full IAM permissions and have the security team remove extra permissions from new roles every week.

explanation.summary: アクセス許可の境界（permissions boundary）は、マネージドポリシーで ID ベースのポリシーが与えられる権限の上限を決める。開発者にロールの作成を任せる時は、境界で任せる権限の上限を決める。境界はそれだけでは権限を与えない。

per_choice.A: 境界は権限を与えないので、他にポリシーの無いロールは何もできない。また開発者自身の境界では、開発者が作るロールの上限にならない。
per_choice.B: アカウント全体の上限になり、広い権限が要る他のチームも止まる。
per_choice.C: 正しい。開発者が作るロールに必ず境界が付くので、どんなポリシーを付けても S3 と DynamoDB の範囲を超えない。
per_choice.D: 人が毎週見直すことになり、要件に反する。見直すまでの間は上限を超えられる。

references.quote: A permissions boundary is an advanced feature for using a managed policy to set the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an IAM entity.
When you delegate permissions to others, use permissions boundaries to set the maximum permissions that you delegate. A permissions boundary does not grant permissions on its own.

questions.stem: An application's IAM role has the AdministratorAccess policy. AWS CloudTrail has recorded the role's activity for the last 90 days. The security team must replace the policy with a fine-grained policy that allows only the actions that the application actually uses. The new policy must be tested in a staging environment before production, and the team wants to avoid writing the policy by hand. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Remove permissions from AdministratorAccess one service at a time in production until the application fails, and keep the last working version.
Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate a policy from the role's CloudTrail activity, test it in staging, and then deploy it to production.
Attach a permissions boundary that allows only the services the team expects, and keep AdministratorAccess on the role.
Read the application's source code to list the API calls, and write a new policy for those actions by hand.

explanation.summary: IAM Access Analyzer は、CloudTrail に残ったアクセスの記録から、ロールが使ったサービスと操作を分析して細かいポリシーを作る。作ったポリシーを試してから本番に出せば、必要な権限だけを与えられる。

per_choice.A: 本番で止まるまで外す方法で、試してから出す要件にも反する。
per_choice.B: 正しい。記録からポリシーを作り、試してから本番に出す。
per_choice.C: 境界は上限を決めるだけで、使った操作だけの細かいポリシーにはならない。予想で決めた上限では、要る操作が抜けたり余分が残ったりする。
per_choice.D: 手で書くことになり、要件に反する。

references.quote: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes the services and actions that your IAM roles use, and then generates a fine-grained policy that you can use.
After you test each generated policy, you can deploy the policy to your production environment.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. The security team must find Amazon S3 buckets and IAM roles in any account whose resource-based policies allow access from principals outside the organization. The team wants a finding for each such resource and does not want to maintain scripts that parse policies. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Use IAM last accessed information in each account to find resources that were used by external principals.
Attach a permissions boundary to every IAM role so that external principals cannot use the roles.
Run a scheduled script that reads every bucket policy and role trust policy and reports external principals.
Use IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust, and review its findings.

explanation.summary: IAM Access Analyzer は、組織やアカウントのリソース（S3 バケットや IAM ロールなど）のうち、外部と共有されているものを見つける。リソースベースのポリシーを論理的に分析し、外部と共有されたリソースごとに検出結果（finding）を作る。

per_choice.A: 最終アクセスの情報は、使っていないユーザー・ロール・権限を見つけて外すためのもので、外部との共有を見つけるものではない。
per_choice.B: 境界は ID ベースのポリシーの上限を決めるもので、外部と共有されているリソースを見つけない。
per_choice.C: 動くが、スクリプトを保守することになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 正しい。リソースベースのポリシーを分析し、外部と共有されたリソースごとに検出結果を作る。

references.quote: IAM Access Analyzer helps you identify the resources in your organization and accounts, such as Amazon S3 buckets or IAM roles, shared with an external entity.
For each instance of a resource shared outside of your account, IAM Access Analyzer generates a finding.
IAM provides last accessed information to help you identify the users, roles, permissions, policies, and credentials that you no longer need so that you can remove them.

questions.stem: An IAM role has an identity-based policy that allows s3:* on a bucket and explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject on the same bucket. The role also has a permissions boundary that allows only s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on that bucket. No other policies apply. Which requests made by the role to the bucket will be allowed? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: s3:GetObject
s3:ListBucket
s3:PutObject
s3:DeleteObject
s3:PutBucketPolicy

explanation.summary: 実際の権限は、ID ベースのポリシーと境界の両方が許す操作（重なり）だけ。どちらかに明示的な拒否があれば、その操作は拒否される。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ID ベースのポリシー（s3:*）と境界の両方が許す。
per_choice.B: ID ベースのポリシーは許すが、境界が許していない。
per_choice.C: 正しい。ID ベースのポリシーと境界の両方が許す。
per_choice.D: ID ベースのポリシーの明示的な拒否が勝つ。境界も許していない。
per_choice.E: ID ベースのポリシーは許すが、境界が許していない。

references.quote: An entity's permissions boundary allows it to perform only the actions that are allowed by both its identity-based policies and its permissions boundaries.
An explicit deny in either of these policies overrides the allow.

questions.stem: A company has 40 project teams, and each team uses an IAM role. Teams create new Amazon S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables every week. Today the security team writes a separate policy for each team that lists the ARNs of the team's resources, and must update the policies whenever a resource is added. The company wants least privilege with fewer policies and no policy updates when resources are added. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Keep one policy per team, and add a script that appends new resource ARNs to the team's policy every night.
Use the AWS managed job function policies for each team so that new resources are included automatically.
Give every team role full access to S3 and DynamoDB, and review access logs each month.
Tag each role and each resource with a project tag, and use one policy that allows access when the principal's tag matches the resource's tag.

explanation.summary: 属性ベースのアクセス制御（ABAC）は、タグという属性で権限を決める。主体のタグとリソースのタグが一致する時に操作を許す 1 つのポリシーで済み、新しいリソースを足してもポリシーを変えなくてよい。従来の役割ベース（RBAC）は職務ごとにポリシーを作り、リソースが増えるたびにポリシーの更新が要る。

per_choice.A: ポリシーの数は減らず、更新をスクリプトで続けることになる。
per_choice.B: 職務別のマネージドポリシーは RBAC の考え方で、プロジェクトごとのリソースに絞れない。
per_choice.C: 最小権限に反する。
per_choice.D: 正しい。1 つのポリシーで、タグが一致するリソースだけに許す。

references.quote: You can design ABAC policies that allow operations when the principal's tag matches the resource tag.
The disadvantage to using the traditional RBAC model is that when you or your users add new resources to your environment, you have to update the policies to allow access to those resources.
ABAC requires fewer policies.

questions.stem: Employees sign in to AWS through IAM Identity Center, and the identity source stores each user's department. Each department's Amazon S3 buckets are tagged with a department tag. Employees must access only their own department's buckets, and the company does not want to create one permission set per department or IAM users. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: On the Attributes for access control page in IAM Identity Center, select the Department user attribute.
In one permission set, add a policy that allows S3 access only when aws:PrincipalTag/Department matches the bucket's department tag.
Create a separate permission set for each department that lists that department's bucket ARNs.
Create an IAM user for each employee and tag the user with the department.
Write the department into each bucket policy as an allowed IAM Identity Center group name.

explanation.summary: IAM Identity Center の Attributes for access control で、ポリシーで使うユーザーの属性（例 Department）を選ぶ。IAM Identity Center はその属性を、入る先のアカウントへセッションタグとして渡し、ポリシーでは aws:PrincipalTag/タグのキー の条件で参照できる。属性がバケットのタグと一致する時だけ許すポリシーを権限セットに書く。

per_choice.A: 正しい。Department の属性をセッションタグとして渡すようにする。
per_choice.B: 正しい。1 つの権限セットで、部署が一致するバケットだけに許す。
per_choice.C: 部署ごとの権限セットを作ることになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.D: IAM ユーザーを作らない要件に反する。
per_choice.E: バケットごとに書き足すことになり、属性で決める仕組みにならない。

references.quote: While on the Attributes for access control page, you select the Department user attribute for use with attribute-based access control (ABAC).
they are sent as session tags that you can reference using the aws:PrincipalTag/tag-key condition key in all relevant AWS IAM policy types.
you then write a policy that grants users access only when the Department attribute matches the department tag that you assigned to your S3 buckets.

questions.stem: A company uses IAM Identity Center with AWS Organizations. Fifteen database administrators need the same RDS, DynamoDB, and Aurora administration permissions in 25 accounts. Staff join and leave the DBA team every month, and the security team wants policy changes to reach all accounts automatically. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create one Database Admin permission set and assign it to each of the 15 administrators individually in all 25 accounts.
Create one Database Admin permission set and assign it to a DBA group in all 25 accounts, repeating the assignment for each batch of up to 10 accounts.
Create an IAM role with the same policies in each of the 25 accounts, and update the 25 roles whenever the policies change.
Create 25 permission sets, one for each account, and assign each to the DBA group.

explanation.summary: 権限セットは 1 つ以上の IAM ポリシーをまとめたテンプレートで、1 つの権限セットで複数のアカウントへのアクセスを与えられる。割り当てると IAM Identity Center が各アカウントにロールを作り、権限セットを変えるとロールとポリシーも更新される。割り当ては個人よりグループにするのが勧められ、1 回に選べるアカウントは 10 まで。

per_choice.A: 人が入れ替わるたびに割り当てを直すことになる。グループに割り当てるのが勧められている。
per_choice.B: 正しい。グループに割り当てれば人の出入りはグループの変更だけで済み、権限セットを変えれば全アカウントに反映される。
per_choice.C: 25 個のロールを自分で保つことになり、手間が大きい。
per_choice.D: 同じ権限を 25 個の権限セットで保つことになり、変更の手間が増える。

references.quote: As you modify the permission set, IAM Identity Center ensures that the corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly.
we recommended that you assign access directly to groups rather than to individual users.
You can select up to 10 AWS accounts at a time per permission set when you assign single sign-on access to users and groups.

questions.stem: A company gives a third-party monitoring vendor access to its AWS account through an IAM role that the vendor assumes. The vendor serves many customers from one AWS account. The company must prevent another customer of the vendor from tricking the vendor into accessing the company's resources by supplying the company's role ARN. Which configuration BEST meets this requirement?

choices.text: In the role's trust policy, allow only the vendor's account, and require an ExternalId value that the company creates and keeps secret.
In the role's trust policy, allow only the vendor's account, without any condition, because only the vendor can assume the role.
Create an IAM user with an access key for the vendor instead of a role, and rotate the key every 90 days.
In the role's trust policy, allow only the vendor's account, and require the ExternalId condition with the unique value that the vendor provides for the company.

explanation.summary: 混乱した代理（confused deputy）は、権限の無い者がより権限のある者に操作をさせる問題。外部 ID をロールの信頼ポリシーの条件で求めると防げる。外部 ID は業者が顧客ごとに一意に作って管理する値で、顧客が自分で決めるものではない。別の顧客が ARN を渡しても、業者が要求に入れる外部 ID は操れない。

per_choice.A: 外部 ID は業者が作って管理する値で、顧客が自分で決めるものではない。
per_choice.B: 業者のアカウントは他の顧客のためにも動くので、別の顧客が ARN を渡すと業者が代わりに入れてしまう。
per_choice.C: 長く使う認証情報を外部に渡すことになり、混乱した代理の問題も解決しない。
per_choice.D: 正しい。業者が顧客ごとに決めた外部 ID を条件にする。

references.quote: The primary function of the external ID is to address and prevent the confused deputy problem.
The ExternalId value must be unique among Example Corp's customers and controlled by Example Corp, not its customers.
Even if another customer supplies Example Corp with your ARN, it cannot control the external ID that Example Corp includes in its request to AWS.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Security Hub CSPM in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. The company sets us-east-1 as the home Region for cross-Region aggregation and links all other Regions. Workloads were recently deployed in ap-south-1, but no findings from ap-south-1 appear in us-east-1. The company wants these findings in the home Region and wants to keep a single place to review them. What should the company do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Wait for cross-Region aggregation to enable Security Hub CSPM in ap-south-1 for each account.
Enable Security Hub CSPM in ap-south-1 for the accounts that have workloads there.
Change the home Region to ap-south-1 so that findings from that Region are collected.
Export findings from ap-south-1 to Amazon S3 each day and import them into us-east-1.

explanation.summary: リージョンをまたぐ集約は、Security Hub CSPM を有効にしているリージョンのデータだけを集める。集約の設定で Security Hub CSPM が有効になることは無いので、ap-south-1 で有効にする必要がある。

per_choice.A: 集約の設定によって Security Hub CSPM が自動で有効になることは無い。
per_choice.B: 正しい。有効にすれば、リンクしたリージョンとしてホームリージョンに集まる。
per_choice.C: ホームリージョンを変えても、ap-south-1 で有効になっていなければデータは集まらない。見る場所も変わってしまう。
per_choice.D: 毎日の書き出しと取り込みの仕組みを作ることになり、手間が大きい。

references.quote: Security Hub CSPM only aggregates data from Regions where an account has Security Hub CSPM enabled.
Security Hub CSPM is not automatically enabled for an account based on the cross-Region aggregation configuration.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. The security team works from a dedicated security account and must manage AWS Security Hub CSPM for every account in the organization. Accounts that join the organization later must be enabled and configured without extra work. The company wants to follow the currently recommended way to manage Security Hub CSPM across an organization. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: From the Organizations management account, designate the security account as the Security Hub CSPM delegated administrator.
Attach a Security Hub CSPM declarative policy to the organization root.
Sign in to each member account and enable Security Hub CSPM in every Region.
Send an invitation from the security account to each new account when it joins the organization.
Make the security account the Organizations management account so that it controls all accounts.

explanation.summary: Organizations と連携すると、管理アカウントが Security Hub CSPM の委任管理者を決める。宣言型ポリシー（declarative policy）は組織のアカウントで Security Hub CSPM をまとめて有効にして設定でき、組織に入ったアカウントや OU に移ったアカウントも引き継ぐ。宣言型ポリシーは、組織全体で管理する推奨の方法として、レガシーになった central configuration に置き換わっている。

per_choice.A: 正しい。委任管理者を決めると、そのアカウントで Security Hub CSPM が自動で有効になり、組織を管理できる。
per_choice.B: 正しい。ルートに付けると、後から入るアカウントも引き継ぐ。
per_choice.C: アカウントごとの作業になり、後から入るアカウントにも同じ作業が要る。
per_choice.D: アカウントが入るたびに作業が要り、要件に反する。
per_choice.E: 管理アカウントを入れ替えることになり、要件に関係無い大きな変更になる。委任管理者を決めれば足りる。

references.quote: When you integrate Security Hub CSPM and AWS Organizations, the Organizations management account designates a Security Hub CSPM delegated administrator.
Accounts that join the organization, or move into an OU that has an attached declarative policy, inherit the declarative policy.
Security Hub CSPM declarative policies replace central configuration as the recommended way to manage Security Hub CSPM across an organization.

questions.note: central configuration はレガシー（2026-11-25 の公式ドキュメント）。試験が古い形のままなら central configuration の選択肢が出る可能性がある

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Control Tower. A detective control is enabled on the Workloads OU. One account in the Workloads OU runs a legacy system that cannot meet the control yet. The company must keep the control for every other account in the OU, must not report this account as noncompliant, and wants to avoid writing custom rules. What should the company do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Disable the control for only the legacy account and keep it enabled for the rest of the Workloads OU.
Disable the control on the Workloads OU and create a custom AWS Config rule for the other accounts.
Move the legacy account to a separate OU where the control is not enabled.
Keep the account in the Workloads OU and suppress the noncompliant results each week.

explanation.summary: Control Tower のコントロールは OU 全体に当たり、OU の中の全てのアカウントが影響を受ける。1 つのアカウントだけを外すには、そのコントロールを有効にしていない別の OU へ移す。

per_choice.A: コントロールは OU の単位で当たり、OU の中の 1 つのアカウントだけを外すことはできない。
per_choice.B: 自分でルールを作ることになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 正しい。別の OU に移せば、そのコントロールは当たらない。
per_choice.D: 毎週の手作業になり、noncompliant と出さない要件にも合わない。

references.quote: A control applies to an entire organizational unit (OU), and every AWS account within the OU is affected by the control.

questions.stem: Web servers in a public subnet accept HTTPS from the internet through a security group. The security team must block one malicious IP address range from reaching any instance in the subnet, while all other HTTPS traffic continues to be allowed. The team wants a network-level control and does not want to change each instance. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Add a deny rule for the IP address range to the security group of the web servers.
Add a deny rule for the IP address range to the subnet's network ACL with a lower rule number than the rule that allows HTTPS.
Add a deny rule for the IP address range to the subnet's network ACL with a higher rule number than the rule that allows HTTPS.
Remove the HTTPS rule from the security group, and add allow rules for every IP address range except the malicious one.

explanation.summary: セキュリティグループは許可のルールだけで、拒否は書けない。ネットワーク ACL は許可と拒否の両方を書け、番号の小さい順に評価し、合ったルールを当てて残りは見ない。拒否のルールは、HTTPS を許すルールより小さい番号にする。

per_choice.A: セキュリティグループには許可のルールしか書けない。
per_choice.B: 正しい。小さい番号の拒否が先に合うので、その範囲だけを止められる。
per_choice.C: 番号の小さい HTTPS の許可が先に合い、拒否のルールは評価されない。
per_choice.D: 許可のルールをたくさん持つことになり、手間が大きく、範囲の管理も難しい。

references.quote: Allow rules only
We evaluate the rules in order, starting with the lowest numbered rule, when deciding whether allow or deny traffic.
If the traffic matches a rule, the rule is applied and we do not evaluate any additional rules.

questions.stem: A team replaced the default network ACL of a subnet with a custom network ACL. The custom ACL has an inbound rule that allows HTTPS from the internet and no outbound rules except the default deny. The instance's security group allows inbound HTTPS. Clients can reach the servers, but they never receive responses. Which change will fix the problem with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Add an outbound rule to the custom network ACL that allows the return traffic to the clients.
Add an outbound rule to the security group that allows responses to the clients.
Add a second inbound HTTPS rule to the custom network ACL with a lower rule number.
Replace the security group with one that has deny rules for all other traffic.

explanation.summary: ネットワーク ACL はステートレスで、前に送受信した通信を覚えていない。入ってくる通信を許すルールを作っても、その応答は自動では許されないので、戻りの通信を出ていく方向のルールで許す必要がある。セキュリティグループはステートフルで、戻りの通信は自動で許される。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ネットワーク ACL は戻りの通信を明示して許す必要がある。
per_choice.B: セキュリティグループはステートフルなので、許した通信の応答は既に通る。止めているのはネットワーク ACL。
per_choice.C: 入ってくる通信は既に許されている。応答が出ていけないのが問題。
per_choice.D: セキュリティグループには拒否のルールは書けず、問題もネットワーク ACL の側にある。

references.quote: If, for example, you create a NACL rule to allow specific inbound traffic to a subnet, responses to that traffic are not automatically allowed.
Automatically allowed (stateful)
Must be explicitly allowed (stateless)

questions.stem: A login API runs behind an Application Load Balancer. Attackers send floods of login requests from a changing set of IP addresses. The company must automatically limit any source that sends requests too fast, without blocking normal users and without writing code or updating IP lists by hand. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Add deny rules for the attacking IP addresses to the subnet's network ACL whenever the attacks are noticed.
Add deny rules for the attacking IP addresses to the load balancer's security group.
Write an AWS Lambda function that reads the access logs every minute and updates an IP block list.
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule with the Application Load Balancer.

explanation.summary: AWS WAF は Application Load Balancer・CloudFront・API Gateway の REST API を守れる。rate-based rule は入ってくるリクエストを数え、速すぎる時に制限する。決めた条件でまとめて数えるので、送り元の IP が変わっても手でリストを直す必要が無い。

per_choice.A: 見つけるたびに人が足すことになり、IP が変わると追い付かない。
per_choice.B: セキュリティグループには拒否のルールは書けない。
per_choice.C: 自分でコードを書くことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 正しい。速すぎる送り元を自動で制限する。

references.quote: A rate-based rule counts incoming requests and rate limits requests when they are coming at too fast a rate.
Application Load Balancer
Allow rules only

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. The security team works from a dedicated security account and must detect communication with known malicious IP addresses and unusual API activity in every member account. The team does not want to create VPC flow logs in each account. When a threat finding appears, analysts must be able to investigate the root cause. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: From the management account, designate the security account as the delegated GuardDuty administrator, and enable GuardDuty for the member accounts.
Use Amazon Detective to investigate GuardDuty findings and identify their root cause.
Create VPC flow logs in every account first, because GuardDuty cannot analyze network traffic without them.
Use Amazon Detective to detect threats in each account, instead of GuardDuty.
Enable GuardDuty only in the security account, because it automatically monitors every account in the organization.

explanation.summary: GuardDuty は既知の悪いドメインや IP との通信、怪しい動きを検出し、CloudTrail の管理イベントや EC2 の VPC フローログのデータを分析する。フローログを自分で作る必要は無い。管理アカウントが委任管理者を決めると、そのアカウントがリージョンの全メンバーの GuardDuty を有効にして管理できる。Detective は、検出結果などから根本の原因を調べるのに使う。

per_choice.A: 正しい。委任管理者がメンバーの GuardDuty を有効にして管理する。
per_choice.B: 正しい。GuardDuty の検出結果から調査を始められる。
per_choice.C: フローログを自分で作らなくても、GuardDuty はデータを分析できる。
per_choice.D: Detective は調べるための物で、検出は GuardDuty などの結果から始まる。
per_choice.E: 委任管理者を決めて、メンバーのアカウントで有効にする必要がある。

references.quote: You don't need to create or configure VPC flow logs in your account for GuardDuty to access this data.
By default, the administrator account can enable and manage GuardDuty for all the member accounts in the organization within that Region.
Amazon Detective makes it easy to analyze, investigate, and quickly identify the root cause of security findings or suspicious activity.
For example, you are assigned to look into findings or alerts uncovered by services such as Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Inspector.

questions.stem: A company has thousands of Amazon S3 buckets. The security team wants ongoing, broad visibility into where sensitive data might be across all buckets without configuring each analysis. The team also needs a deeper, targeted analysis of three regulated buckets every month, with custom criteria on object properties. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Turn on Macie automated sensitive data discovery for the account.
Create a recurring Macie sensitive data discovery job that targets the three regulated buckets with custom criteria.
Create a one-time sensitive data discovery job over all buckets, because it keeps monitoring new objects afterward.
Rely on automated sensitive data discovery to analyze every object in the three regulated buckets in full depth.
Create a custom data identifier for each bucket so that Macie monitors the bucket continually.

explanation.summary: Macie は 2 つの方法で機密データを見つける。自動の機密データの発見は、S3 のバケットの一覧を続けて評価し、サンプリングで代表のオブジェクトを選んで、広く見える化する。機密データの発見ジョブは、対象のバケット・サンプリングの深さ・オブジェクトの性質の条件を決める、より深く絞った分析で、一度だけか定期で動かせる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。設定を作り込まずに、全てのバケットを続けて広く見る。
per_choice.B: 正しい。3 つのバケットを、条件を決めて毎月深く調べる。
per_choice.C: 一度だけのジョブはその時の分析で、その後の監視はしない。
per_choice.D: 自動の発見はサンプリングで代表のオブジェクトを選ぶ物で、全てを深く調べる物ではない。
per_choice.E: カスタムデータ識別子は見つける条件の定義で、バケットを監視する仕組みではない。

references.quote: With this option, Macie continually evaluates your S3 bucket inventory and uses sampling techniques to identify and select representative S3 objects from your buckets.
Sensitive data discovery jobs provide deeper, more targeted analysis.
You can configure a job to run only once for on-demand analysis and assessment, or on a recurring basis for periodic analysis, assessment, and monitoring.

questions.stem: A company's internal employee IDs follow the pattern EMP- followed by six digits and must be reported by Amazon Macie as sensitive data. Test files in the same buckets contain well-known sample credit card numbers that the team does not want reported, while real credit card numbers must still be reported. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Use only the managed data identifiers, because they already detect employee IDs and ignore sample card numbers.
Create an allow list for the employee ID pattern, and a custom data identifier for the sample card numbers.
Create a custom data identifier with a regex for the employee IDs, and an allow list that contains the sample card numbers.
Turn off the managed data identifier for credit card numbers, and create a custom data identifier for the employee IDs.

explanation.summary: カスタムデータ識別子は、正規表現などで会社独自の機密データを見つける条件を決め、マネージドデータ識別子を補う。許可リスト（allow list）に入れた文字や形は、マネージドやカスタムの識別子の条件に合っても報告されない。

per_choice.A: マネージドデータ識別子は決まった種類の機密データを見つける物で、会社独自の社員 ID の形は知らない。
per_choice.B: 逆になっている。許可リストに入れた物は報告されなくなる。
per_choice.C: 正しい。社員 ID は独自の条件で見つけ、サンプルの番号だけを許可リストで外す。
per_choice.D: 本物のカード番号も報告されなくなる。

references.quote: The criteria consist of a regular expression (regex) that defines a text pattern to match and, optionally, character sequences and a proximity rule that refine the results.
If data matches text or a text pattern in an allow list, Macie doesn’t report the data.
This is the case even if the data matches the criteria of a managed data identifier or a custom data identifier.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with 50 member accounts. The security team must manage Amazon Macie centrally from a security account, review S3 bucket information for member accounts, and enable Macie for member accounts without signing in to each one. Which approach BEST meets these requirements?

choices.text: Send Macie membership invitations from the security account to all 50 accounts, and have each account owner accept them.
Sign in to each member account to enable Macie, and share the findings with the security team by email.
Enable Macie only in the security account, because it automatically scans buckets in every member account.
Integrate Macie with AWS Organizations, designate the security account as the Macie administrator, and enable Macie for the member accounts from it.

explanation.summary: Macie の組織は、指定した Macie の管理者アカウントとメンバーアカウントでできる。つなぎ方は AWS Organizations との連携か、Macie の招待で、Organizations との連携が勧められている。Organizations でつないだ場合、Macie の管理者はメンバーアカウントで Macie を有効にでき、メンバーの S3 バケットの情報も見られる。

per_choice.A: 動くが、各アカウントで受け入れる作業が要り、勧められている方法でもない。
per_choice.B: 各アカウントに入る必要があり、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 管理者とメンバーの関係を作らないと、他のアカウントのバケットは見られない。
per_choice.D: 正しい。勧められている Organizations との連携で、管理者が各メンバーで有効にできる。

references.quote: We recommend that you integrate Macie with AWS Organizations.
If the accounts are associated through AWS Organizations, the Macie administrator can also enable Macie for member accounts in the organization.
Tasks include reviewing information about S3 buckets that are owned by member accounts, reviewing policy findings for those buckets, and inspecting the buckets for sensitive data.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations and is a new AWS CloudTrail customer. The security team works from a dedicated security account and must record events for the management account and every member account, including accounts that join later. The security team must manage the logging configuration without signing in to the management account. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Use CloudFormation StackSets to create a separate trail in every member account, and add the stack to new accounts when they join.
Create an organization trail in the management account, and give the security team an IAM role in the management account to manage it.
Create a CloudTrail Lake event data store for the organization in the security account, and query events from there.
From the management account, make the security account a CloudTrail delegated administrator, and create an organization trail from the security account.

explanation.summary: 組織の証跡（organization trail）は、管理アカウントと全メンバーアカウントのイベントを記録する。管理アカウントは委任管理者を決められ、委任管理者は組織の証跡を作って管理できるので、セキュリティのチームは管理アカウントに入らずに済む。

per_choice.A: アカウントごとに証跡を持つことになり、新しいアカウントへの追加の作業も要る。
per_choice.B: 記録はできるが、セキュリティのチームが管理アカウントに入ることになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: CloudTrail Lake は 2026 年 5 月 31 日から新しい利用者の受付を止めており、新しく使い始める会社には選べない。
per_choice.D: 正しい。委任管理者として組織の証跡を作り、管理アカウントにも入らない。

references.quote: The management account for the organization can assign a delegated administrator to create new organization trails or manage existing organization trails.
Organization trails log events for the management account and all member accounts in the organization.
AWS CloudTrail Lake will no longer be open to new customers starting May 31, 2026.

questions.stem: An auditor requires the company to prove that AWS CloudTrail log files in Amazon S3 were not modified or deleted after delivery. The auditor also wants proof that no log files were delivered during a specific period when no activity occurred. The company wants to rely on a built-in CloudTrail capability instead of building its own process. What should the company do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Turn on CloudTrail log file integrity validation, and validate the log files with the hourly files that CloudTrail delivers.
Turn on S3 Versioning for the log bucket so that every change to a log file keeps an earlier version.
Write an AWS Lambda function that stores a hash of each new log file in Amazon DynamoDB, and compare the hashes during audits.
Send the trail to Amazon CloudWatch Logs as well, and compare the events in both places during audits.

explanation.summary: ログファイルの整合性の検証を有効にすると、CloudTrail は届けた全てのログファイルのハッシュを作り、1 時間ごとにその時間のログファイルとハッシュを並べたファイルも届ける。これで、届けた後の変更・削除・偽造を見つけられ、ある期間にログファイルが届けられなかったことも言える。

per_choice.A: 正しい。CloudTrail の機能だけで、変更・削除の有無と、届けられなかった期間を示せる。
per_choice.B: 変更の前の版は残るが、どれが CloudTrail の届けたままのファイルかや、ある期間に届けられた物が無いことは示せない。
per_choice.C: 自分で仕組みを作ることになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 比べる手間がかかり、届けた後に変えられていないことの証明にはならない。

references.quote: When you enable log file integrity validation, CloudTrail creates a hash for every log file that it delivers.
Every hour, CloudTrail also creates and delivers a file that references the log files for the last hour and contains a hash of each.
assert positively that no log files were delivered to your account during a given period of time.

questions.stem: A company stores audit logs in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. No user, including the root user, may overwrite or delete any log object for 7 years. Some log objects are part of a legal investigation and must be kept beyond 7 years, for as long as the investigation lasts. The investigation team must be able to release those objects when the investigation ends. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Set a default retention period of 7 years in compliance mode for the bucket.
Set a default retention period of 7 years in governance mode for the bucket.
Place a legal hold on the investigation objects, and give the investigation team the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission.
Place a legal hold with a fixed period of 10 years on the investigation objects.
Give the investigation team permission to bypass governance mode so that they can extend retention when needed.

explanation.summary: compliance モードでは、保持期間の間、ルートユーザーを含め誰もオブジェクトの版を上書きも削除もできない。法的保持（legal hold）は期間を持たず、外されるまで続き、s3:PutObjectLegalHold の権限を持つ人が付け外しできる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ルートユーザーも含めて 7 年間は上書きも削除もできない。
per_choice.B: governance モードは、特別な権限を持つ人なら削除や設定の変更ができるので、「誰も」の要件に合わない。
per_choice.C: 正しい。調査が続く間は残り、調査のチームが外せる。
per_choice.D: 法的保持には決まった期間が無い。外されるまで続く。
per_choice.E: governance モードでは誰も消せないことにならない。期間を延ばすのは法的保持で足りる。

references.quote: In compliance mode, a protected object version can't be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the root user in your AWS account.
In governance mode, users can't overwrite or delete an object version or alter its lock settings unless they have special permissions.
However, a legal hold doesn't have an associated fixed amount of time and remains in effect until removed.
Legal holds can be freely placed and removed by any user who has the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with 40 accounts in four Regions, and AWS Config records resources in every account. The security team needs one view of configuration and compliance data for all accounts and Regions from its security account. The security account must not be able to change anything in the source accounts, and the team does not want to approve access in each account one by one. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create an AWS Config aggregator in the security account that uses the organization as its source.
Create an AWS Config aggregator in the security account that lists each account, and authorize it in every source account.
Create an IAM role with AWS Config write permissions in every account, and switch to each role to review the data.
Write an AWS Lambda function that copies configuration snapshots from every account to the security account each day.

explanation.summary: アグリゲーターは、許された元のアカウントとリージョンのデータを集約アカウントへ写し、読むだけの見え方を作る。元のアカウントやリージョンを変える権限は持たない。AWS Organizations の一部のアカウントを集める時は、承認が要らない。

per_choice.A: 正しい。組織を元にすれば各アカウントでの承認が要らず、読むだけで変えられない。
per_choice.B: 読むだけの見え方は作れるが、アカウントごとに承認する作業が要り、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 書き込みの権限を与えることになり、変えられない要件に反する。1 つの見え方にもならない。
per_choice.D: 自分で仕組みを作ることになり、手間が大きい。

references.quote: Aggregators provide a read-only view into the source accounts and Regions that the aggregator is authorized to view by replicating data from the source accounts into the aggregator account.
Aggregators do not provide mutating access into a source account or region.
Authorization is not required if you are aggregating source accounts that are part of AWS Organizations.

questions.stem: A security team wants to be alerted when the rate of API calls that create resources suddenly rises far above the account's normal pattern, without defining fixed thresholds. The account has a trail that logs only read management events. The team enabled CloudTrail Insights for API call rate on the trail a week ago, but no Insights events have appeared, although unusual activity occurred. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm with a static threshold on the number of CreateInstance calls in the trail's log group.
Configure the trail to also log write management events, keep Insights enabled, and allow up to 36 hours for Insights events to start.
Create a new event data store with Insights for data events, because Insights does not work on trails.
Move the trail to us-east-1, because Insights events are generated only in that Region.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail Insights は、過去のイベントから API の呼び出しの率と誤りの率のふつうの形（基準）を作り、それから大きく外れた時に Insights のイベントを出す。管理イベントの呼び出しの率で Insights のイベントを出すには、証跡が書き込みの管理イベントを記録している必要がある。初めて有効にした後、出し始めるまで最大 36 時間かかることがある。

per_choice.A: 決まったしきい値を決めることになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 正しい。書き込みの管理イベントを記録しないと、管理イベントの呼び出しの率の Insights は出ない。
per_choice.C: データイベントの Insights は証跡でしか使えない。今回の問題は書き込みの管理イベントを記録していないこと。
per_choice.D: Insights のイベントは、元になる管理イベントやデータイベントと同じリージョンで出る。

references.quote: To log Insights events on the API call rate for management events, the trail or event data store must enable Insights and log write management events.
After you enable CloudTrail Insights for the first time on a trail, CloudTrail may take up to 36 hours to begin delivering Insights events
Insights events on data events are only supported on trails and not on event data stores.
A CloudTrail Insights event is generated in the same Region as its supporting management or data event is generated.

questions.stem: A custom metric counts failed sign-in attempts. Its normal value changes strongly by hour of day and day of week, so static thresholds either miss attacks at night or raise false alarms during business hours. The security team wants an alarm only when failures are unusually high for that time, not when they are unusually low. Which alarm BEST meets these requirements?

choices.text: A static threshold alarm set to the highest value seen during business hours.
An anomaly detection alarm that triggers when the metric is either above or below the band.
An anomaly detection alarm that triggers when the metric is above the band of expected values.
An anomaly detection alarm that triggers when the metric is below the band of expected values.

explanation.summary: 異常検知（anomaly detection）では、統計と機械学習で過去のデータから期待される値の範囲（バンド）を作る。異常検知のアラームは決まったしきい値を持たず、その時の期待値と比べる。バンドより上・下・どちらでも、のどれで鳴らすかを選べる。

per_choice.A: 決まったしきい値で、夜の攻撃を見逃し、時間帯による変化に合わない。
per_choice.B: 少なすぎる時にも鳴り、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 正しい。その時間帯にしては多すぎる時だけ鳴る。
per_choice.D: 少なすぎる時に鳴り、多すぎる時には鳴らない。

references.quote: These types of alarms don't have a static threshold for determining alarm state.
You can choose whether the alarm is triggered when the metric value is above the band of expected values, below the band, or both.

questions.stem: A company uses GuardDuty with a delegated administrator account. The security team wants an email for each new finding and wants repeated occurrences of an existing finding to be reported every 15 minutes instead of every 6 hours. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule for GuardDuty findings with an Amazon SNS topic that has an email subscription as the target.
In the GuardDuty administrator account, set the notification frequency for subsequent finding occurrences to 15 minutes.
In each member account, set the notification frequency for subsequent finding occurrences to 15 minutes.
Change the notification frequency for newly generated findings from 6 hours to 15 minutes.
Turn on email notifications in GuardDuty, which sends findings by email without an EventBridge rule.

explanation.summary: GuardDuty は検出結果を EventBridge へ自動で送る。通知を受けるには EventBridge のルールとターゲット（例えば SNS のトピック）を作る。新しい検出結果はほぼリアルタイムに送られ、その頻度は変えられない。同じ検出結果のその後の発生は既定で 6 時間ごとにまとめられ、管理者アカウントだけが 15 分・1 時間・6 時間から変えられる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ルールのターゲットに SNS のトピックを置き、メールで受ける。
per_choice.B: 正しい。その後の発生の頻度は管理者アカウントが 15 分にできる。
per_choice.C: 頻度を変えられるのは管理者アカウントだけ。
per_choice.D: 新しい検出結果はほぼリアルタイムで送られ、この頻度は変えられない。
per_choice.E: 通知を受けるには EventBridge のルールとターゲットを作る必要がある。

references.quote: In order to receive notifications about GuardDuty findings based on events, you must create an EventBridge rule and a target for GuardDuty.
Only an administrator account can update the EventBridge notification frequency for subsequent finding occurrences.
Possible values are 15 minutes, 1 hour, or the default 6 hours.
The notification frequency for newly generated findings is in near real-time.

questions.stem: Auditors must see who downloaded objects from one sensitive Amazon S3 bucket. The account's trail logs only management events, and the account has hundreds of other busy buckets. The company wants to capture the needed activity while keeping CloudTrail costs as low as possible. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Enable data events on the trail with advanced event selectors that match only that bucket and the GetObject operation.
Enable data events on the trail for all S3 buckets in the account.
Keep the current trail, because management events already record GetObject calls on objects.
Enable CloudTrail Insights on the trail so that unusual download activity is recorded.

explanation.summary: 証跡は既定ではデータイベントを記録しない。データイベントは S3 のオブジェクトへの GetObject などのリソースの操作で、量が多く追加の料金がかかる。高度なイベントセレクター（advanced event selectors）で細かく絞れば、必要なイベントだけを記録して費用を抑えられる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。必要なバケットと操作だけに絞って記録する。
per_choice.B: 忙しい他のバケットのイベントも記録し、費用が増える。
per_choice.C: GetObject のようなオブジェクトの操作はデータイベントで、既定では記録されない。
per_choice.D: Insights は API の呼び出しの率の異常を見る物で、誰がオブジェクトを取ったかの記録にはならない。

references.quote: By default, trails and event data stores do not log data events. Additional charges apply for data events.
Amazon S3 object-level API activity (for example, GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject API operations) on objects in S3 buckets.
You can use advanced event selectors to create fine-grained selectors, which help you control costs by only logging the specific events of interest for your use cases.

questions.note: 選択肢 D の Insights の説明は C-0079 の出典（Insights は API の呼び出しの率と誤りの率）による

questions.stem: A security team wants records of every rejected connection attempt to the network interfaces in one subnet, stored in Amazon S3 for later queries. The records should be aggregated at the shortest interval that VPC Flow Logs supports. Accepted traffic should not be recorded. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Create a flow log for the subnet that captures rejected traffic and publishes to Amazon S3.
Set the flow log's maximum aggregation interval to 1 minute.
Set the flow log's maximum aggregation interval to 30 seconds.
Create a flow log that captures all traffic and publishes directly to Amazon OpenSearch Service.
Keep the default maximum aggregation interval, which is the shortest interval available.

explanation.summary: フローログは VPC・サブネット・ネットワークインターフェイスに作れ、記録する通信の種類（受け入れ・拒否・全て）と送り先を決める。送り先は CloudWatch Logs・S3・Data Firehose。集計の最大の間隔は既定で 10 分で、作る時に 1 分にできる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。サブネットの拒否された通信だけを S3 に送る。
per_choice.B: 正しい。1 分が選べる最も短い間隔。
per_choice.C: 選べるのは既定の 10 分か 1 分。
per_choice.D: 送り先は CloudWatch Logs・S3・Data Firehose で、受け入れた通信も記録してしまう。
per_choice.E: 既定は 10 分で、最も短い間隔ではない。

references.quote: The type of traffic to capture (accepted traffic, rejected traffic, or all traffic)
Flow log data can be published to the following locations: Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Data Firehose.
By default, the maximum aggregation interval is 10 minutes. When you create a flow log, you can optionally specify a maximum aggregation interval of 1 minute.

questions.stem: During a security review, a company finds that it has no record of the HTTP requests that reached its Application Load Balancer, and no central copy of the application log files that are written to local disks on its Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants both kinds of logs collected with managed features. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Enable access logs on the Application Load Balancer and specify an Amazon S3 bucket for them.
Install the CloudWatch agent on the instances and configure it to send the application log files to CloudWatch Logs.
Find the existing access logs in the load balancer's console, because access logs are always on.
Enable VPC Flow Logs, which record the HTTP request paths that reach the load balancer.
Enable CloudTrail management events, which copy the application log files from the instances.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing のアクセスログは既定で無効の任意の機能で、有効にすると指定した S3 バケットに圧縮したファイルで置かれる。CloudWatch エージェントは、EC2 のインスタンスやオンプレミスのサーバーからログを集めて CloudWatch Logs に送る。VPC フローログはネットワークインターフェイスの IP の通信の情報を記録する物。

per_choice.A: 正しい。既定で無効なので、有効にして S3 に置く。
per_choice.B: 正しい。エージェントがインスタンスのログを CloudWatch Logs に集める。
per_choice.C: アクセスログは既定で無効。
per_choice.D: フローログは IP の通信の情報で、HTTP のリクエストの中身は記録しない。
per_choice.E: CloudTrail の管理イベントは AWS の操作の記録で、インスタンスのログファイルは集めない。

references.quote: Access logs is an optional feature of Elastic Load Balancing that is disabled by default.
In all three models, the agent collects logs from Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers into Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC.
